excerpt: guilds.run is an open-source, self-hosted platform for teams of AI agents where you can inspect every prompt, tool call and memory change. Licence, setup, planned hosted pricing and alternatives.
content:
guilds.run runs standing teams of AI agents that you can see inside. A guild is a team of agents, each with its own role, model and tools, sharing a chat, notes and tables. Agents wake up on a schedule, through a routine, or when a person or another agent calls them. Every run keeps the exact prompt the model saw, every tool call and its result, every memory change and who wrote each note, so you can trace how one agent's mistake carried into the next agent's work.

A built-in assistant called Studio reads a live team's runs, notes and memory and drafts fixes for you to review; nothing changes until you publish. Each agent gets a sandboxed workspace with a terminal, reusable scripts and an optional browser. You can pick a different model for each agent, from Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok to open-weight models through OpenRouter, DeepInfra or Ollama, using your own keys. Connectors include Notion, Gmail, Google Drive, GitHub and X, with Slack, Linear, Google Calendar and LinkedIn listed as coming soon. Teams can be exported as recipe files.

guilds.run is open source under the AGPL-3.0 licence and runs on your own machine with Docker. A hosted version is announced but not yet available. It is made by Cigale AI and launched on Product Hunt on 12 October 2026, finishing #4 for the day with 193 upvotes and 46 comments.

We have not tested guilds.run ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing page and GitHub README, its Product Hunt page and the official pricing pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.platform: Self-hosted web app (Docker); hosted version coming
profile.os: Self-hosting needs Docker; bring your own model API keys
profile.starts_at: Free to self-host; hosted version announced from $19/month
profile.summary_short: Open-source, self-hosted platform for AI agent teams where every prompt and tool call is inspectable
use_cases: Running a team of agents for ongoing work such as growth, sales research or support
Tracing where a multi-agent workflow went wrong, run by run
Monitoring mentions across social platforms into a shared table (templates for this were promised at launch)
Mixing models, with a different model for each agent
Testing a workflow before letting agents run it for real

paragraphs: Emmanuel Chappat says getting AI to handle long-running tasks reliably takes more than good prompts. It is a system-design problem: deciding how agents work together, anticipating edge cases, and being able to debug and tune things when they go wrong.

guilds.run is built to make the whole system understandable, so you can trace how mistakes spread between agents, fix the cause and check whether the fix worked. The team open-sourced it to see what others build and to share working teams for real use cases. At launch he announced two next steps: sharing recipes for whole agent teams, and a hosted mode.
launch_story.attribution: Emmanuel Chappat, maker, on Product Hunt

fit: run multi-agent workflows and need to see exactly what each agent did
are comfortable self-hosting with Docker and using your own model keys
want open source and the freedom to choose a model per agent
not_fit: want a hosted service today: it is announced but not open yet
need Slack, Linear, Google Calendar or LinkedIn connectors now (listed as coming soon)
can't use AGPL-licensed software in your setup

pricing.intro: Self-hosting is free under the AGPL-3.0 licence; you pay your model providers. A hosted plan is announced but not yet available.

plans.name: Self-hosted
plans.detail: Run it yourself with Docker; bring your own model API keys

plans.name: Hosted (coming soon)
plans.detail: Full product, sign-in with Google or an email link, team invites, public recipe directory; model usage on platform keys billed separately

notes: The running costs shown on example recipes (for example around $2.10 a day for an X growth team) are estimates of model usage, not plans.
Trial and refund terms are not published.

alternatives.intro: Product Hunt lists LangChain, Langfuse, Dify and other AI infrastructure; we compared guilds.run with the closest agent-team tools. Prices come from each product's own pricing page, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: CrewAI
items.what: Framework and platform for multi-agent crews
items.starts_at: Basic free (50 workflow runs a month); Enterprise custom
items.difference: A Python framework with a managed cloud. guilds.run is a self-hosted app with a UI, shared notes and tables, and full run records for each agent.

items.name: LangGraph and LangSmith
items.what: LangChain's agent orchestration framework with hosted deployment and tracing
items.starts_at: Developer $0 (1 seat); Plus $39 per seat a month
items.difference: Code-first for developers. guilds.run offers ready team templates and an operator app.

items.name: n8n
items.what: Workflow automation with AI agent nodes, self-hostable
items.starts_at: Starter €20/month billed yearly; free self-hosted Community Edition
items.difference: Node-based automation with hundreds of integrations, rather than persistent agent teams with memory and run inspection.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Langfuse, Dify.AI, Helicone AI and GPTBots.ai.

liked: Self-hosting plus visibility into every tool call, which commenters linked to trust
Debugging tools for people who aren't developers
asked: Coordinating agents across X, Reddit, LinkedIn and Instagram into one spreadsheet (templates promised)
Whether a hosted version is coming (yes, soon)
How it copes when agents on different models depend on each other's outputs

pros: Open source and free to self-host
Full record of prompts, tool calls and memory changes for every run
Different model per agent, including local models through Ollama
Studio drafts fixes from real runs, and nothing changes until you publish
Connectors are opt-in per organisation, team or agent
cons: Very new: the GitHub repository was created on 9 October 2026
Needs Docker and your own model keys
AGPL-3.0 licence may not suit every company
Several popular connectors are still coming soon

x.none: We found no independent posts about guilds.run on X to link yet. The team posts updates as @guildsrun.

faq.a: Yes, to self-host. It is open source under the AGPL-3.0 licence and you pay only your model providers. A hosted version is announced from $19 a month but isn't open yet.

faq.q: What do I need to run it?
faq.a: Docker. Clone the repository, run the setup script, start it with Docker Compose, open it in your browser and paste a model API key, as the README describes.

faq.q: Which AI models can agents use?
faq.a: Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok, and open-weight models such as Qwen, DeepSeek, Kimi, Llama, Mistral and GLM through OpenRouter, DeepInfra or Ollama. Each agent can use a different model.

faq.q: Can I test a workflow before it runs for real?
faq.a: Yes. The maker said on Product Hunt that his co-founder does this all the time when building workflows.
Not yet. The team says it is coming soon and invites people to leave an email on the site.
Cigale AI, according to the README.
